## Proposed boundaries and flow

An application factory composes a Flask web adapter, server-rendered Jinja templates, a recovery service, a synthetic account store, a reset-request/token store, a session registry, a clock, and an in-memory notification sink. The stores and sink may share one injected in-process state object and lock so eligibility and completion decisions have consistent atomic boundaries. Flask renders HTML on the server; there is no public account-inventory, notification-sink, or token-inspection endpoint. Static assets may style the observed sign-in surface but do not determine recovery behavior. The in-memory sink is accessible to tests/internal fixtures, never visitors. [STORY, IMAGE, STANDARD; REQ-001–REQ-014]

Proposed route/template interface (route names and copy are design choices, **not** supplied visual facts):

| HTTP boundary | Input and contract | Rendered outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /sign-in` | No recovery input. | Server-render `sign_in.html` with the observed sign-in hierarchy and an actual `href` to `GET /password/forgot`; do not claim a working sign-in or particular successful-login destination. |
| `GET /password/forgot` | No account lookup. | Server-render a labeled request form. Recovery-page styling/copy remains provisional. |
| `POST /password/forgot` | Form `email` plus CSRF proof; validate general form shape independently of account existence. | For otherwise equivalent valid existing, unknown, and at-limit account requests, return the **same visible status, template, copy, navigation, and response class**, for example an identical generic confirmation. Never embed whether a link was issued. A malformed form may get a uniform field-specific format error independent of whether that email exists. |
| `GET /password/reset/<token>` | Opaque token in the link; validate without consuming it. | Render a labeled new-password form for an eligible token, otherwise a non-success state with a way to request another link. No token echoed in visible copy. Eligibility on GET is not a reservation. |
| `POST /password/reset/<token>` | `new_password` plus CSRF proof; recheck token eligibility at submission time. | On successful completion, render/redirect to a server-rendered success state with sign-in navigation. Malformed, consumed, or expired tokens give non-success without password change or false success. Password policy is an unresolved choice: do not invent a mandatory complexity rule; reject empty input and keep password values out of logs and responses. |

The wireframe implies only the sign-in rendering, not actual authentication; should a sign-in handler be implemented later, its authentication/authorization rules and success destination require separate clarification. Proposed accessible UI behavior from `ui_analysis` includes persistent programmatic labels, logical keyboard order, visible focus, associated actionable errors, accessible neutral progress/confirmation and non-success states. Treat these as design proposals to verify, not observed features or an invented mandated recovery-page layout. [IMAGE, STORY, STANDARD; REQ-001–REQ-003, REQ-006–REQ-010]

Service boundary contracts:

- `request_reset(normalized_email, now) -> PublicRequestOutcome`: same public outcome regardless of existing/unknown/at-limit; internally, locate a synthetic account and count its requests within the preceding rolling hour. When allowed, record the request, generate a token, store its digest with `issued_at=now`, and append a reset-link notification directed to the account's synthetic email. Never return the token or internal eligibility to the web presenter. Tests can inspect the sink. [STANDARD, STORY; REQ-003–REQ-005, REQ-011, REQ-012]
- `check_link(raw_token, now) -> eligible | ineligible`: hash the supplied token, look up a stored digest, and check unused status and `now < issued_at + 30 minutes`. At the exact expiry instant it is **ineligible**. A rendered GET never marks it used. [STANDARD; REQ-006, REQ-007]
- `complete_reset(raw_token, new_password, now) -> success | ineligible | invalid_input`: compute a password hash, then under a shared lock **recheck** token, account, and current time; on success replace the account's stored hash, consume that token, advance the account's session-revocation generation, and record **one owner-directed success notification for this success**. Return success only after these in-process effects are recorded. Two concurrent POSTs for one token cannot both succeed. No notification for rejected/replayed submissions. A process crash cannot make these in-memory steps durable; this is explicitly not a distributed transaction. [STANDARD, STORY; REQ-006–REQ-010, REQ-012]
- `is_session_active(session_id, account_id) -> bool` must require a live server-side session record and a matching account generation. A successful reset advances the generation under the same completion lock, so **every pre-existing session for that account is rejected on its next access**, including when there are multiple sessions or a stale client cookie persists. Fixtures may create multiple synthetic active sessions to exercise REQ-009 without asserting that sign-in success was specified or building an unrelated login product. If the implementation later supports login, every authenticated request must use this check; merely clearing the browser that submitted the reset is insufficient. [STANDARD; REQ-009]

## State and data contracts

| Internal record | Minimal fields and invariants |
| --- | --- |
| Synthetic `Account` | Internal stable `account_id`, normalized email key, password **hash** (never plaintext), monotonic `session_generation`. No external directory or real account integration. |
| `ResetRequest` | `account_id`, accepted request timestamp. Count timestamps strictly newer than `now - 1 hour`; at the boundary a prior request falls out. At most five accepted existing-account requests within the preceding hour produce links; the sixth produces none but the same generic public response. Define/count these under the same lock as issuance to prevent concurrent over-issuance. Unknown-account emails are not persisted as accounts. |
| `ResetToken` | Digest of a cryptographically random opaque URL token, `account_id`, exact UTC `issued_at` captured **when issued**, `used` flag. Use `now < issued_at + 30 minutes`, not request, notification, or first-open time. Raw token appears only in the private sink's reset-link entry and the request URL, not token storage, application logs, or generic responses. |
| `Session` | Unpredictable server-side ID, `account_id`, generation at creation, active/revoked state if maintained. A browser cookie is only an ID, not a self-sufficient authorization grant; checks consult server-side state and account generation. Sessions may be introduced via test fixtures until sign-in semantics are resolved. |
| `Notification` | Internal `kind=reset_link | reset_success`, owner recipient, timestamp, and link **only** for `reset_link`; successful-reset notice has no new password or reset token. Each successful completion appends one owner-directed `reset_success`; tests may count entries. No real mail delivery guarantee. |

Normalize submitted email consistently (e.g., trim and case-fold for lookup) and validate syntax before lookup; do not reveal whether lookup succeeded. Inject a timezone-aware UTC clock so fixed-time tests can exercise the rolling-hour rollover and just-before/exactly-at/after-expiry boundaries. Keep the one-process state coherent through an application-scoped store and lock; restart discards accounts, rate counters, tokens, session state, and notifications. **Migration:** none for the exercise's volatile data. Before any production substitution, design durable account/token/request/session/notification storage, transactional or outbox-backed effects, retention, key management, data migration, and cross-worker consistency separately; none of that is authorized implementation or a deployment target here. [STORY, STANDARD; REQ-003–REQ-012, REQ-016]

## Decisions and alternatives

| Decision | Alternative considered | Reason / qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python 3.12 Flask application factory and Jinja server rendering. | SPA/client-only rendering or other framework. | Directly serves approved runtime and rendered-HTML constraints without inventing a frontend architecture. [STORY; REQ-013, REQ-014] |
| One injectable, synchronized in-memory state container for synthetic accounts, rolling request timestamps, token digests, sessions, and notifications. | External database, identity provider, cache, or mail service. | Testable, cohesive exercise boundary, not production-safe durability or delivery; a single lock guards check-and-write operations. Multi-process workers would break these guarantees and are unsupported. [STORY, STANDARD; REQ-003–REQ-012] |
| Cryptographically random opaque links (e.g., Python `secrets.token_urlsafe`), store only a SHA-256 digest, compare/check under lock; issue-time UTC clock determines expiry. | Sequential tokens, plaintext token table, or expiry based on request/open/send time. | Limits guessability and exposure, enforces single-use and the exact 30-minute issue-time boundary. Protect URL-bearing logs and referrers as well as token storage. [STANDARD; REQ-006, REQ-007] |
| Per-account rolling one-hour accepted-request timestamps, strictly within `(now − 1 hour, now]`, with the same generic public presentation. | Fixed clock-hour bucket, per-IP-only throttling, or distinct “account throttled” page. | A rolling interpretation makes “preceding hour” deterministic and avoids boundary bursts and account enumeration. Additional global abuse defenses would need separate policy, not a substitute for the account cap. [STANDARD; REQ-003, REQ-004] |
| Hash new passwords using a maintained Flask-compatible password hashing utility (for example Werkzeug's `generate_password_hash`); never keep cleartext as account state. | Plaintext or reversible encryption, external identity integration. | Limits exposure in this exercise without claiming a specified password-complexity or sign-in policy. Verify selected hash algorithm/tooling in implementation. [STORY; REQ-008, REQ-011] |
| Server-side session registry checked against an account revocation generation, advanced on every successful reset. | Clear only current browser cookie or rely entirely on stateless signed cookies. | Invalidation reaches all active sessions rather than only the resetting browser; injected multiple-session fixtures demonstrate the invariant without assuming login success semantics. [STANDARD; REQ-009] |
| Synchronous internal notification records of two distinguishable kinds; success shown only after the reset effects and notice are committed in-process. | Actual email delivery or success page treated as proof of notification. | Meets the inspectable sink and after-every-success requirement without external integration; crash durability/delivery is unproven. [STORY, STANDARD; REQ-005, REQ-010, REQ-012] |

## Security, reliability, and operations

- Route POSTs should use CSRF protection tied to a browser session, including the unauthenticated request and reset forms; the link is not itself a CSRF defense. Require an application secret from configuration (no checked-in credential), safe session-cookie attributes, escaping in server templates, and suitable content/referrer policy for token URLs. Generate absolute reset links from a configured trusted origin, **not** an unchecked Host header. Avoid token-bearing URLs in access logs, analytics, referrer leakage and public error pages. These are proposed defensive implementation choices, not claims of standards beyond STANDARD. [STORY, STANDARD; REQ-003, REQ-006–REQ-008]
- Authorization for a reset is possession of an eligible single-use token, independent of sign-in; do not allow a token to name a different account via user input. Password change, token consumption, session-generation increment and success notification occur for the token's stored account under one critical section. Recheck at POST even after a successful GET; invalid/replayed/expired requests must neither update passwords nor invalidate sessions nor generate success notices. Use a generic non-success link state without echoing token material. [STANDARD; REQ-006–REQ-010]
- Treat public-response equality as status, headers/redirect destination, rendered content, and visible form state for equivalent valid submissions; unknown or at-limit paths must not leak through account-specific copy or a link/sink endpoint. Exact network timing equivalence is not established by these notes: equalize obvious branching where feasible and state timing-based enumeration as a production limitation. Request counters and notices are volatile; no retry or delivery guarantee across process failure. For a memory/notification failure, do not present a false successful reset; tests should cover consistent state where possible. [STANDARD, STORY; REQ-003–REQ-005, REQ-010, REQ-016]
- Minimal local structured observability: count generic request attempts, link issuance, throttling, successful and rejected resets, and sink-record failures internally, with no submitted email, raw token, password, or link URL in logs. Public responses must remain account independent. No external telemetry backend or operational deployment is authorized; instrumentation is for local testability/diagnosis, not evidence of production monitoring. [STORY, STANDARD; REQ-003, REQ-015, REQ-016]
- Documentation must name synthetic accounts, ephemeral single-process persistence, non-delivered in-memory notifications, missing production account integration, rate limits lost at restart, lack of cross-worker coordination/durability, and unresolved production security/ops hardening. Do not deploy or create/edit deployment workflows. [STORY; REQ-016–REQ-018]

## Open questions / explicit assumptions

1. **Sign-in and sessions:** Neither IMAGE nor the approved requirements specifies a login-success destination, authentication rules, or an existing session implementation. Interim design: supply a generation-checked session interface and multiple-session fixtures for REQ-009; if real login is later defined, bind every authenticated access to that check. Do not infer login behavior from a button in the wireframe. [IMAGE, STANDARD; REQ-001, REQ-009]
2. **Recovery UI:** Exact request/reset/invalid/success copy, layout, and style are unknown. Apply IMAGE only to sign-in; use accessible functional recovery states as explicitly proposed in `ui_analysis`, pending product clarification. [IMAGE, STORY; REQ-002, REQ-006–REQ-008]
3. **Password rules:** No new-password complexity policy, confirmation field, or minimum length was supplied. Interim design validates presence, hashes the password, and leaves further policy open rather than labeling a guessed rule mandatory. [STORY; REQ-008]
4. **Production decisions:** No durable store, delivery provider, deployment topology, or other organizational architectural standard is authorized/found. The in-process architecture is an exercise limitation; production changes would require a separate design and approval. [STORY; REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-016–REQ-018]
